data.current_description: SYNC size-reducer: a scanned PDF (or images) in -> a much smaller, SEARCHABLE PDF out, returned directly. Small docs only (larger -> async /v1/book). Billed 1 credit/page. output="same" makes the result follow the input: a SINGLE image in gives a recompressed image back (JPEG, or PNG when the source needs alpha) with no OCR and no text layer — because "shrink this photo" shouldn't hand back a PDF. Multiple images, or any PDF, always produce a PDF; output="pdf" (the default) always does. grayscale=True (THE DEFAULT) does NOT convert the document to greyscale. It drops the chroma planes only where a page — or, on a PDF whose own JPEG streams are rewritten, an individual strip — carries no real colour, judged by connected coloured AREA rather than an average. A stamp, a signature, a logo or a coloured rule keeps its colour; blank margins and black text lose planes that held nothing. Worth about -6% on a text scan for nothing visible. Send grayscale=false to keep every plane regardless. vectorize=True additionally erases the original raster text (LaMa inpaint) and redraws it as real vector text at the same position — much smaller for text-heavy pages and crisp at any zoom. Because a misread becomes a permanent, visible error in that mode (unlike the invisible search layer), any line the OCR wasn't confident about gets one more independent verification pass (reverify_lines), and anything still uncertain is flagged with a PDF comment so the user can check it against the source.

Suitable for small documents only; use /v1/book for larger files. Billed at 1 credit per page. Supports three output modes: output="same" preserves input format (single image returns recompressed image; multiple images/PDFs return PDF), output="pdf" (default) always returns PDF. Optional parameters: grayscale=true (default) selectively removes color information from non-colored areas while preserving colored elements like logos and signatures; vectorize=true converts raster text to vector text for smaller file size and crisp rendering, with additional verification and flagging of uncertain OCR results. Requires authentication.

data.current_description: SYNC size-reducer: a scanned PDF (or images) in -> a much smaller, SEARCHABLE PDF out, returned directly. Small docs only (larger -> async /v1/book). Billed 1 credit/page. output="same" makes the result follow the input: a SINGLE image in gives a recompressed image back (JPEG, or PNG when the source needs alpha) with no OCR and no text layer — because "shrink this photo" shouldn't hand back a PDF. Multiple images, or any PDF, always produce a PDF; output="pdf" (the default) always does. grayscale=True (THE DEFAULT) does NOT convert the document to greyscale. It drops the chroma planes only where a page — or, on a PDF whose own JPEG streams are rewritten, an individual strip — carries no real colour, judged by connected coloured AREA rather than an average. A stamp, a signature, a logo or a coloured rule keeps its colour; blank margins and black text lose planes that held nothing. Worth about -6% on a text scan for nothing visible. Send grayscale=false to keep every plane regardless. vectorize=True additionally erases the original raster text (LaMa inpaint) and redraws it as real vector text at the same position — much smaller for text-heavy pages and crisp at any zoom. Because a misread becomes a permanent, visible error in that mode (unlike the invisible search layer), any line the OCR wasn't confident about gets one more independent verification pass (reverify_lines), and anything still uncertain is flagged with a PDF comment so the user can check it against the source.
data.summary_suggestion: Synchronously compress and make documents searchable
data.description_suggestion: Synchronously compresses and optimizes scanned PDFs or images into smaller, searchable documents with OCR text layer. Returns result directly (not async). Suitable for small documents only; use /v1/book for larger files. Billed at 1 credit per page. Supports three output modes: output="same" preserves input format (single image returns recompressed image; multiple images/PDFs return PDF), output="pdf" (default) always returns PDF. Optional parameters: grayscale=true (default) selectively removes color information from non-colored areas while preserving colored elements like logos and signatures; vectorize=true converts raster text to vector text for smaller file size and crisp rendering, with additional verification and flagging of uncertain OCR results. Requires authentication.
